record.paper_title: Spin-density-functional theory: some open problems and application to inhomogeneous Heisenberg models
record.original_question: What are the ground-state and time-dependent consequences, and what functional approximations are needed, for the exchange-correlation torque that arises in noncollinear spin-density-functional theory beyond the local-spin-density approximation when the exchange-correlation magnetic field has a component perpendicular to the spin magnetization?

evidence.quote: This perpendicular xc magnetic field exerts an xc torque ∝ m(r)× Bxc(r) on the spin distribution. In the time-dependent case some consequences of this torque were described in [18], but it is present even in the ground state as soon as noncollinearity appears and is treated beyond the LSDA. This subtle effect is little explored in present-day SDFT.

The existence of spin currents, providing a link between SDFT and CDFT; the existence of an exchange-correlation torque appearing in noncollinear spin configurations; and the nonuniqueness of the potentials of SDFT and other generalized DFTs are examples of the kind of surprise the SDFT formalism still holds.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. In noncollinear spin-density-functional theory (SDFT) the basic variables are the electron density n(r) and the vector spin magnetization m(r) ∈ ℝ³. The Kohn–Sham equations are governed by an effective scalar potential v_s(r) and an effective magnetic field B_s(r) = B_ext(r) + B_xc(r), where the exchange-correlation magnetic field is the functional derivative B_xc(r) = −δE_xc[n,m]/δm(r) of the exchange-correlation energy functional E_xc[n,m]. The local-spin-density approximation (LSDA) takes E_xc^LSDA[n,m] = ∫ ε_xc(n(r), |m(r)|) dr, which yields B_xc^LSDA(r) parallel to m(r) at every point, so that the local torque density

  τ_xc(r) := m(r) × B_xc(r)

vanishes pointwise. Beyond LSDA (e.g. for general gradient or nonlocal approximations), B_xc(r) generically has a component perpendicular to m(r), giving rise to a nonzero local exchange-correlation torque τ_xc(r). The "zero-torque theorem" requires only that the integrated torque ∫ m(r) × B_xc(r) dr vanish for the exact functional.

Problem. Carry out a systematic analysis of the exchange-correlation torque τ_xc(r) = m(r) × B_xc(r) in noncollinear SDFT beyond LSDA. Specifically:

(a) Ground state. Identify the physical consequences of a nonvanishing local xc torque on the static Kohn–Sham solution: characterize how it modifies the equilibrium spin texture m(r) compared to LSDA, and determine general constraints (such as the global zero-torque condition ∫ m × B_xc dr = 0, gauge invariance under global SU(2) spin rotations, and the correct collinear limit) that any admissible functional E_xc[n,m] must satisfy.

(b) Time-dependent case. In time-dependent noncollinear SDFT with Kohn–Sham equation iħ ∂_t Ψ = [H_0 + σ · B_s(r,t)] Ψ, determine the consequences of the local xc torque for spin-precession and magnetization dynamics, in particular for the continuity equation ∂_t m + ∇ · J_spin = m × B_s, and clarify whether and how τ_xc enables damping or dissipative spin dynamics within an adiabatic-type approximation.

(c) Functional approximations. Construct (or prove obstructions to constructing) explicit semilocal or orbital-dependent approximations to E_xc[n,m] that (i) reproduce LSDA in the collinear limit, (ii) are invariant under U(1) charge and SU(2) spin gauge transformations, (iii) yield a nonvanishing local torque τ_xc(r) where appropriate while respecting the global zero-torque theorem, and (iv) are numerically stable in self-consistent calculations.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of designing noncollinear xc functionals beyond LSDA that yield a well-behaved local exchange-correlation torque has seen substantial progress but remains active. Recent works (Phys. Rev. B 107, 165111 (2023); Phys. Rev. Research 5, 013036 (2023); arXiv:2501.04124 (2025); arXiv:2504.15024 (2025)) propose semilocal, multicollinear, and orbital-dependent constructions that produce nonvanishing local xc torques, respect gauge invariances, satisfy the global zero-torque theorem, and capture spin-torque dynamics. However, no single approximation is universally accepted, and numerical stability and the correct collinear limit remain ongoing challenges, so the broader question—including the full ground-state and time-dependent consequences—is only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Constructing semilocal approximations for noncollinear spin density functional theory featuring exchange-correlation torques
status_evidence.snippet: semilocal exchange-correlation energy functional ... derived for noncollinear magnetism, is U(1) and SU(2) gauge invariant, and gives rise to nonvanishing exchange-correlation torques.
status_evidence.claim: Recent semilocal constructions beyond LSDA produce nonzero xc torques satisfying gauge invariance, indicating partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Noncollinear density functional theory
status_evidence.snippet: The multicollinear approach satisfies the correct collinear limit ... provides global zero torque, satisfying the zero torque theorem.
status_evidence.claim: A multicollinear framework addresses collinear limit and zero-torque theorem, showing the area is actively developing.

status_evidence.title: Capturing spin-torque effects with a semilocal exchange-correlation functional
status_evidence.snippet: semilocal exchange-correlation functional ... captures spin-torque effects
status_evidence.claim: Spin-torque effects can be captured by recent semilocal functionals, addressing the time-dependent aspect.

status_evidence.title: Operator Formalism for Noncollinear Functionals in Multicollinear Approach
status_evidence.snippet: different schemes can produce nonzero xc torques, but they tend to suffer from numerical instabilities
status_evidence.claim: Numerical stability of local xc torque schemes is still an open practical issue.
